text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The boom in capital expenditure over the last 18 months in corporate Australia has produced some of the biggest profit slumps since the recession. The rise in expenditure is expected to generate higher profits and justify record stock prices but has hit cmpanies hard with higher depreciation and interest expenses associated with major investments. Page 1.

The value of projects on which Australia's banks and other financiers acted as advisers rose 45 per cent to nearly A$41 billion last year. The result of a rash of privatisation projects and the resurgence of the resources industry, the prject boom has not translated into easy money for the project finance industry due to competition for advisory work and market domination of a small number of large deals. Page 1.

After announcing on Friday the A$312 million sale of its European business, Meneba BV, to venture capital group CVC Capital Partners BV, Goodman Fielder Ltd chief executive David Hearn is looking towards acquisitions, increased capital expenditure and even a capital return to shareholders to make the balance sheet work harder. Page 15.

In Rupert Murdoch's second failure in 12 months to enter the German television market, talks have collapsed between his 40 per cent-owned BSkyB and Germany's Kirch Group. BSkyB had been negotiating to buy up 49 per cent of Kirch's 17-channel DFI digital roadcaster. Page 17.

Brierley Investments Ltd - one of the major shippers between Australia and New Zealand to the US West Coast and also of the main ocean carriers between Australia and New Zealand - says it is looking at buying the Government-owned Australian National Line s part of an expansion of its shipping business. Page 17.

On the eve of a new set of drilling results from Helix Resources Ltd's Tunkillia deposit in South Australia, Acacia Resources revealed in a substantial shareholder notice on Friday it has bought 472,000 Helix shares in the past three weeks, topping up its stake in the company to 18.5 per cent. Page 19.
THE AUSTRALIAN

After a survey of 1,000 bank customers in Australia's major capital cities revealed 65 per cent of those surveyed found the concept of Retirement Savings Accounts appealing, the big banks are preparing for an outright assault on the A$250 billion superannation market. Through RSAs, banks will be able to offer a superannuation deal in a bank account. Page 17.

In a move which threatens to delay development of junior miner Ross Mining NL's Gold Ridge gold project in the Solomon Islands, Melbourne law firm Slater & Gordon, who acted for landowners in the Ok Tedi dispute with BHP, is expected to lodge two Ok Tedi-tyle actions with the Solomon Islands High Court today. Page 17.

The Maralinga Tjarutja people - the nearest permanent community to the former nuclear test site - have formed a joint venture to explore for gold and other minerals in the productive Gawler Craton. The joint venture agreement is between Resolute ResourcesLtd, Dominion Mining Ltd and MT Mining Pty, a company established by the Maralinga people, and covers tenements on 5,000 square kilometres adjacent to the Challenger deposit. Page 17.

An urgent meeting will be held in Melbourne tomorrow by the board of Bougainville Copper Ltd to discuss the future of its dormant Panguna copper mine, which is BCL's only asset. The Papua New Guinea Government has yet to formally approach RTZ-CRA with an offer to buy its majority stake. Page 19.

As part of a plan to expand its worldwide beer marketing activities, Foster's International, which describes itself as "the blue blur behind the Formula One cars", has announced it has revised its contract with the Formula One Constructors Association. Foster's now has exclusive "pouring rights" for nine of the 17 rounds in this year's world drivers' championship, as well as signage rights for 11 races which will be viewed by millions around the world. Page 19.

According to figures from accounting firm Ernst & Young, there are significant variations between the performances of the States regarding business failures. The figures show the number of businesses going insolvent in the December quarter rose 15 per cen on the previous corresponding period, with Victoria and Tasmania accounting for a combined 38 per cent of the national total. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Australian arm of News Corporation has commissioned adviser Baring Bros Burrows to seek a buyer for its 50 per cent stake in Australian Newsprint Mills, Australia's primary supplier of newsprint, as part of a A$1 billion assets sales plan announced last month. Page 37.

In a move which will expand its rapidly growing European markets and spearhead a push into South America, Foster's has struck a deal with Formula One, worth about A$20 million, which grants the brewer exclusive rights to provide beer at the upmarket Formula One Paddock Club at each Grand Prix and exclusive "pouring rights" at nine Grands Prix this year. Page 37.

After signing just a handful of customers since its local phone call market was launched last June, Optus Vision's 46.5 per cent owner US West has told the other shareholders - Optus Communications, Publishing and Broadcasting and Seven Network - the inital software problems have been corrected. Optus Vision has delayed a full-scale marketing and installation program while its improved software is being commercially tested over the next month. Page 37.

New Zealand Brierly Investments was yesterday targeting the Australian Government owned Australian National Line (ANL) as part of an expansion of its shipping business. Brierly chief executive Paul Collins said the purchase would enhance the company's othr shipping interests in the Australian region. Page 39.

An exploration deal covering the South Australian Gawler Craton exploration ground has been struck between the Resolute Resources and Dominion Mining DOM.AX partnership and the Maralinga Tjarutja people. The agreement covers 5,000 kilometres of Maralinga freehold and puts the Aboriginals in joint venture with Resolute/Dominion - the partnership that triggered the gold exploration rush to Gawler. Page 39.

Publishing and Broadcasting PBL.AX managing director James Packer has moved to take advantage of the Indian Government's moves towards privatising a faltering arm of its national television network, Doordarshan. Packer met Information and Broadcasting Minister Irahim about two weeks ago, reportedly to express interest in investing in Doordarshan 3, the national broadcaster's upmarket channel. Page 37.
THE AGE

Managing director of News Ltd Lachlan Murdoch says scrapping cross-media ownership rules and restraining foreign ownership restrictions will not create diversity in the industry, but will give some current players increased power. Murdoch said possible moes by the Federal Government to drop existing cross-media laws were "only going half-way" in its review of ownership laws, and that the government should "open the rules across the board" to encourage diversity and competition. Page B1.

Former Bond Corp director Tony Oates is attempting to cut a deal with Australian authorities which will see him voluntarily return to Perth after spending more than four months in a Polish jail. Oates has instructed his Sydney lawyer Mark Webeck to put adeal to the Federal Attorney-General's Department and the Commonwealth Director of Public Prosecutions to see him released from jail in Gdansk to return to face corporate fraud charges. Page B1.

Grand Prix motor racing business Formula One is planning a global stockmarket listing valued at around A$5 billion. The move will make a billionaire of owner Bernie Ecclestone, and looks set to send shockwaves through global motor racing - one of the world's most lucrative sports. Despite reports of uneasiness over team revenue distribution, international financial institutions are expected to back the offer. Page B1.

A deal which gives Foster's exclusive "pouring rights" at nine Grand Prix this year has been estimated at A$20 million. The deal grants exclusive rights to provide beer at the upmarket formula-one Paddock Clubs, and features increased track signage and prmotion through the official programs. The company will use the deal to expand in Europe and South America. Page B1.

Brisbane-based gold producer Union Mining NL has outlined plans to merge with America's Yamana Resources Inc in a A$30 million scheme of arrangement. Under the deal, Yamana, subject to the company completing financing arrangements, will pay 20 cents for ach Union share, and six cents for each option. Page B2.

New Zealand based Brierley Investments chief executive Paul Collins has identified Government-owned Australian National Line as a possible acquisition target in the company's expansion in Australia. Collins said the acquisition would enhance Brierley's oher shipping interests in the region. Page B3.
